text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - Shares fell as stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs data sent U.S. stocks and bonds sharply lower amid fresh fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates. The FTSE 100 ended 30.4 points lower at 4,056.6, down 32.9 since last Friday and its lowest close for three weeks.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended a turbulent day of trading lower in electronic trade as Wall Street opened lower despite having earlier hit a record close in Frankfurt bourse trade. The IBIS DAX index came off earlier lows to end the day at 2,915.81 points. Evidence of the see-saw nature of the day's trade lay in the fact that the DAX-30 index earlier ended bourse trade at a record 2,933.39 points, up 40.76 points on the day and a rise of 74.11 on the week.

PARIS - Stocks finished lower after a robust U.S. jobs report hurt Wall Street stocks by fanning concerns about the outlook for U.S. interest rates. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 21.58 points at 2,327.50, up 44.74 for the week.

ZURICH - Shares ended lower, led down by stronger than expected U.S. December jobs data. Until the data, the market had moved sideways. Dealers said fears of rising interest rates pressured financial shares, while industrial stocks saw profit-taking. Losses were mainly a consolidation of recent gains. The all-share SPI fell 12.58 points to 2,526.61 a gain of 14.57 on the week.

TOKYO - Stocks plunged again, buckling under the weight of worries over the economy and the troubled banking sector. The market's key index racked up its largest one-day fall in two years. After plunging more than 950 points with less than an hour of trading left, the benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading companies managed to regain some ground by the close. It ended down 770.22 points at 17,303.55, its lowest level since August 1995 and a fall of 2,057.8 since the end of 1996 trading. The market was closed last Friday.

HONG KONG - Property stocks took another hit, dragging the Hang Seng Index to a lower close, with a fresh slide in Japanese stocks also weighing on sentiment. The blue-chip index fell 6.61 points to 13,191.50, a loss of 31.29 on the week. Turnover was HK$11.33 billion compared with HK$11.41 billion on Thursday.

SYDNEY - The share market closed lower as nervousness over U.S. jobs data and the temptation to take profits overwhelmed early enthusiasm that saw the market scale new heights. The All Ordinaries index fell 4.6 points to 2,418.6. This was 20.2 points off its early record high of 2,438.8 points which it reached in the first hour of trading. There was a gain of 19.1 from last Friday's close.

JOHANNESBURG - Concerns about possible big losses on U.S. markets after stronger-than-expected job creation data spooked South African industrial stocks which, although ending firm, slid well off earlier highs. The industrial closed up 19.2 points at 8,039.3, up 162.8 from a week ago. The gold index added 31.7 points to end at 1,421.8, down 36.2 on the week. The all-share index finished 26.7 points better at 6,674.6 up 77.1 since last Friday.
